failure-message: healthy pull and catch-up must progress while slow pull retains partial state
fix: Give each round a deadline and a byte/event budget decided in ACL2 (a round past it fails and holds the cursor), or run rounds per peer on separate bounded workers so one peer cannot hold the scheduler.
notes: 2026-10-03 Groundwork explicitly authorized shared ACL2/native resumable transport capability; Runtime confirmed IO/owner API disjoint. S067 push-feed fairness and DNS availability remain separate frontiers unless actually consumed. No host wall cap or reused output/cold funding.

Implemented one-attempt TCP/TLS and retained pull/catch-up worker state; raw kernel/worker tests pass. PRF-1260 source/guard certification and actual saved-image SCN-1090 remain pending. No DNS deadline, push fairness, whole-round expiry or context-funding claim.
reviewer: host/native/pull-service.lisp:433-442: the round loop ends only when the session is done or on stop. receive (:422-430) uses +fnn-pull-read-seconds+ (60, :40) per read, and there is no overall round deadline or byte budget anywhere in pull-service.lisp, peer-pull.lisp or peer-pull-session.lisp. fnn-pull-worker (:525-548) runs fnn-pull-round for one due peer at a time, then fnn-catchup-tick (:500-520), which runs its round synchronously on the same thread. A peer that sends at least one octet every 60 s (or lists endlessly in :list, which compounds finding 1) holds the single worker, so every other pull and catch-up round stalls. The pull peers are operator-configured, which caps the severity at medium.
scenario: A pulled peer that trickles one octet every 59 seconds (a slow link or a deliberate slow-loris), or streams an endless ARTICLE body in :forward, keeps its round alive indefinitely. No other pull peer's NEWNEWS round and no catch-up round runs meanwhile, so their cursors stall and their articles are not pulled. The schedule's per-peer interval is meaningless while the worker is held.
title: One pull worker serves every peer serially with only a per-read timeout, so one slow peer starves all pull and catch-up rounds
